violation_type.title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))
violation_type.short_title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization
violation_type.typical_finding: During the investigation, it was determined that the staff was aware of a child receiving medical attention after sustaining an injury while in care, but did not report to Child Care Licensing within two days of becoming notified.

finding_variants.text: During the investigation, it was determined that the staff was aware of a child receiving medical attention after sustaining an injury while in care, but did not report to Child Care Licensing within two days of becoming notified.
The director did not report an injury incident within the required two calendar days.
Operation did not report to licensing that a child was injured at operation that needed medical attention.
During an investigation it was determined that a child in care was injured and required medical attention, but the incident was never reported to Childcare Regulation.
During the investigation, it was determined that the operation failed to notify CCR of a child injury that received medical treatment within the required timeframe.
Information obtained throughout the investigation shows the operation failed to report an incident where a child required medical treatment within the required two-day timeframe.
